# Partial Pre-Rendering (PPR) / Shell Optimization — Codebase Report ## 1. Framework and Version | Item | Value | |------|--------| | **Framework** | Next.js (App Router) | | **Version** | `16.3.0-canary.81` | | **React** | `19.1.0` / `react-dom` `19.1.0` | | **TypeScript** | `^5` | | **Router** | App Router only (`/workspace/app`) — no `pages/` directory | Source: `/workspace/package.json` ```json "dependencies": { "next": "^16.3.0-canary.81", "react": "19.1.0", "react-dom": "19.1.0" } ``` This is **Next.js 16 canary**, where classic `experimental.ppr` / `experimental_ppr` are **removed**. PPR is enabled via the unified **`cacheComponents`** flag. --- ## 2. PPR / Cache Components Configuration **Key file:** `/workspace/next.config.ts` ```1:7:/workspace/next.config.ts import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, } export default nextConfig ``` ### What this means (from Next 16 docs in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`) - `cacheComponents: true` enables: - Component/function-level caching via `'use cache'` - **Partial Prerendering (PPR) as default** for App Router - Dynamic data by default; opt into caching explicitly - The old flags are gone: - ~~`experimental.ppr`~~ - ~~`experimental_ppr` route segment config~~ - ~~`experimental.dynamicIO` / `experimental.useCache`~~ (replaced by `cacheComponents`) From the docs: > Cache Components implements **Partial Prerendering (PPR)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed. > Next.js prerenders a **static HTML shell** that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready. **Search results in app code:** no matches for `ppr`, `experimental_ppr`, `unstable_noStore`, `connection()`, `use cache`, `Suspense`, skeleton components, or streaming comments. Only: - `cacheComponents: true` in config - A coarse `loading.tsx` spinner --- ## 3. App Directory Structure ``` /workspace/app/ ├── layout.tsx # Root layout (static shell base) ├── page.tsx # Dashboard page (blocks on one fetch) ├── loading.tsx # Full-page loading fallback ├── CardStats.tsx # Presentational (receives props) ├── RevenueChart.tsx # Presentational (receives props) └── LatestInvoices.tsx # Presentational (receives props) ``` No nested routes, no route groups, no skeletons directory, no shared UI lib. --- ## 4. Current Shell Structure ### Root layout — static shell candidate (minimal) ```1:18:/workspace/app/layout.tsx import type { Metadata } from 'next' export const metadata: Metadata = { title: 'Create Next App', description: 'Generated by create next app', } export default function RootLayout({ children, }: Readonly<{ children: React.ReactNode }>) { return ( {children} ) } ``` - Pure static: no cookies/headers/fetch - Becomes part of the prerendered shell - No nav, sidebar, or chrome that could enrich the shell ### Page-level loading — only Suspense boundary today ```1:8:/workspace/app/loading.tsx export default function Loading() { return (

Loading dashboard...

) } ``` With App Router, `loading.tsx` auto-wraps `page.tsx` in Suspense: ``` layout (static shell) └── Suspense fallback={loading.tsx} └── page.tsx ← entire page is dynamic hole ``` **Problem:** the shell is only `/` + a full-page spinner. The `

Dashboard

` and layout structure of the dashboard are **not** in the static shell. ### Page — single blocking data fetch (anti-pattern for PPR) ```1:24:/workspace/app/page.tsx import { RevenueChart } from './RevenueChart' import { LatestInvoices } from './LatestInvoices' import { CardStats } from './CardStats' async function getDashboardData() { const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/dashboard') return res.json() } export default async function Page() { const data = await getDashboardData() return (

Dashboard

) } ``` Issues for PPR / shell optimization: 1. **Top-level `await`** on the whole page → nothing under the page can be in the static shell except via `loading.tsx`. 2. **One waterfalled fetch** for all sections → no parallel streaming of cards / chart / invoices. 3. **Presentational children** get data as props; they never fetch themselves, so they cannot be independent Suspense boundaries. 4. **No `'use cache'`** — under Cache Components, uncached `fetch` is dynamic every request (correct for live dashboards, but should stream behind granular Suspense). 5. **No explicit ``** — only the implicit boundary from `loading.tsx`. ### Presentational components (not async, no Suspense) | File | Role | |------|------| | `/workspace/app/CardStats.tsx` | Renders revenue + invoice counts from props | | `/workspace/app/RevenueChart.tsx` | Renders revenue list from props | | `/workspace/app/LatestInvoices.tsx` | Renders invoice list from props | They are fine as pure UI; the optimization is to make **async server components that fetch** and wrap those (or convert these to async fetchers). --- ## 5. How PPR Is Effectively Configured Today | Layer | Status | |-------|--------| | `cacheComponents: true` | Enabled — PPR on | | Static shell content | Minimal (`html`/`body` + loading spinner) | | Explicit `` | None | | `loading.tsx` | Yes — coarse full-page fallback | | `'use cache'` / `cacheLife` | None | | Parallel data boundaries | None — single `getDashboardData()` | | Runtime APIs (`cookies`, etc.) | None | | Nested routes / layouts | None | **Effective user experience:** 1. Build/prerender: static shell = layout + loading spinner fallback. 2. Request: shell served instantly; entire dashboard waits on one API call, then swaps the whole loading UI for the full page. That is PPR technically, but **not optimized**. --- ## 6. What Could Be Optimized Aligned with Next 16 docs (`streaming.md`, `08-caching.md`, `loading.md`, `cacheComponents.md`): ### A. Maximize static shell (highest impact) - Keep page **sync** (or only await static pieces). - Put static UI outside Suspense: `

Dashboard

`, grid chrome, section titles. - Move each data section into its own async Server Component + ``. **Target pattern** (from Next docs streaming guide): ```tsx // Ideal structure for this codebase export default function Page() { return (

Dashboard

{/* static shell */} }> {/* async, fetches own data */} }> }>
) } ``` ### B. Split the monolithic fetch Replace: ```ts async function getDashboardData() { const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/dashboard') return res.json() } ``` With per-section fetches (or three parallel functions), each inside the component that needs it, so sections stream independently as they resolve. ### C. Improve fallbacks (skeleton UI) Current `loading.tsx` is a generic spinner. Prefer: - Section skeletons matching `CardStats` / chart / invoices layout - Optionally keep a thin `loading.tsx` for navigations, or remove it if granular Suspense covers the page (still useful for client navigations) ### D. Optional caching with `'use cache'` If some dashboard data can be stale: ```ts export async function getRevenue() { 'use cache' cacheLife('minutes') // or 'hours' const res = await fetch('...') return res.json() } ``` Cached results can enter the static shell / prefetch; uncached stays dynamic and streams. ### E. Enrich the root layout shell Add shared chrome (nav, sidebar, footer) to `layout.tsx` so it is always in the prerendered shell and stays interactive while page content streams. ### F. Avoid blocking the page root Docs: *“If you `await` at the top of a layout or page, everything below becomes dynamic and cannot be prerendered as part of the static shell.”* Current `page.tsx` does exactly that with `await getDashboardData()`. ### G. Remove or refine `loading.tsx` once granular Suspense exists - With only page-level loading, the shell cannot include the dashboard heading/structure. - With sibling Suspense boundaries, the shell can include real layout + section skeletons. --- ## 7. Key File Paths (absolute) | Path | Relevance | |------|-----------| | `/workspace/package.json` | Next 16.3 canary, React 19 | | `/workspace/next.config.ts` | `cacheComponents: true` (PPR) | | `/workspace/app/layout.tsx` | Root static shell | | `/workspace/app/page.tsx` | Blocking dashboard fetch | | `/workspace/app/loading.tsx` | Only Suspense fallback today | | `/workspace/app/CardStats.tsx` | Presentational section | | `/workspace/app/RevenueChart.tsx` | Presentational section | | `/workspace/app/LatestInvoices.tsx` | Presentational section | | `/workspace/tsconfig.json` | Standard Next TS config | | `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/05-config/01-next-config-js/cacheComponents.md` | Official PPR/cacheComponents docs | | `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md` | Static shell + granular Suspense | | `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/08-caching.md` | Streaming uncached data patterns | | `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/loading.md` | `loading.js` behavior | | `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/migrating-to-cache-components.md` | Migration from old PPR/segment configs | | `/workspace/node_modules/next/AGENTS.md` | Agent note: read local docs; APIs differ from training data | --- ## 8. Relevant Code Snippets Summary **Config enabling PPR (Next 16 model):** ```3:5:/workspace/next.config.ts const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, } ``` **Current anti-pattern (blocks entire page shell content):** ```10:12:/workspace/app/page.tsx export default async function Page() { const data = await getDashboardData() ``` **Only shell fallback:** ```1:8:/workspace/app/loading.tsx export default function Loading() { return (

Loading dashboard...

) } ``` --- ## 9. Bottom Line This is a **minimal Next.js 16 canary dashboard demo** with PPR **enabled but not leveraged**: - **Configured:** `cacheComponents: true` → PPR + Cache Components on. - **Shell today:** bare layout + full-page spinner. - **Gap:** one top-level await fans out data to three presentational widgets; no granular Suspense, no section skeletons, no `'use cache'`. - **Optimization path:** push data fetching into async section components, wrap each in `` with matching skeletons, keep static chrome (`h1`, layout, structure) outside Suspense so it is part of the prerendered static shell and streams independently. session_id: ses_0b8105052ffevkks4G8IwAX7Qt
